Sounds like the pilot opted for a visual landing and then military continued their exercise and the airport had an AWOS fault that made an instrument approach illegal. Alot of things stacked against the pilots. Communication, particularly being able to understand what the other person is experiencing was important here. Pilots are in a vulnerable cognitive situation here. 

Unfortunately with GPS jamming becoming more prevalent TAWS should move to non GPS based systems. I think all the commercial airliners and most fancy planes have these features. Avionics saves so many lives each year and flying under only visual is incredibly dangerous particularly as people become dependent on instruments.

Every year some bozo Dr who thinks they can fly with their ipad as a map because it works 90% of the time gets lost when the thing fails and they have to radio for help.

The average person has little to no clue about what aviation is like and it's rife for misunderstanding, thus fertile psyop ground. I remember that helicopter crash where the pilot moved too quickly and the rotors hit the boom and people were like "can't they just not design it that way?" No, not without introducing more design issues. Helicopters are horrible.

Yea, this came up at a family gathering recently.  I think the average person has a concept of "air travel" in their mind, and it's considered "safe."  Unless they've been told by an expert (pilots usually), they make no distinction between different types of planes or helicopters.

Successful psyop to make air travel appear safe looking only at the big commercial flights with multiple redundant systems while general aviation has about the same risk as driving. Also funny so many stats make it by distance traveled when take off and landing is the most dangerous stretch.
Also crazy how much gps jamming isn't to block GPS but to make misleading data to control the plane/drone.
Yeah, way more variation on planes than cars and not like you can hop into whatever plane and go as easily as a car. I swear everyone should try to take off and land in a sim to see what it's like.
